name: Hiram
overview: Hiram was a male figure known for his significant role in the construction of Solomon's temple, as recorded in 1 Kings 7:14. Though his tribal affiliation is not specified, his work on the temple marks him as an important contributor to Israel's sacred architecture. No additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Hiram means '[my] brother is elevated,' a proper name noted in 1 Kings 7:13. This meaning reflects a name of honor or esteem but is not indicated to be given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Hiram as a descendant of Naphtali according to 1 Kings 7:14. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Hiram's importance in the biblical narrative centers on his skilled labor in building Solomon's temple, a pivotal project in Israel's history that symbolized God's dwelling among His people. His connection to the tribe of Naphtali situates him within the broader Israelite community, highlighting the cooperation involved in fulfilling God's purposes. Through his craftsmanship, Hiram contributed to the physical and spiritual foundation of Israel under Solomon's reign.
